{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABc_QbPw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhGhkyo", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 140, "title": "Implement hardware-accurate per-instruction CPU cycle timing for V30 and i486 profiles", "body": "## Problem

The emulator currently accounts for a fixed **8 scheduler clocks for every instruction / REP element**, regardless of opcode, operand form, or memory/I/O behavior:

```rust
let result = self.cpu.step_with_observer(&mut self.bus, &mut before_instruction);
self.bus.tick(8);
```

See [`src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/lib.rs) and [`docs/hardware.md` § CPU and scheduler](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/hardware.md#cpu-and-scheduler), which explicitly calls this a deterministic scheduling model, **not instruction-cycle accuracy**.

This cannot represent the actual execution time of the target CPUs. Fast register operations, memory/I/O instructions, branches, string operations, interrupts and expensive instructions all receive the same elapsed time. As a result, elapsed guest time relative to graphics, PIT, sound, disk and IRQ activity may be incorrect. In particular, slow screen transitions in games are worth investigating, although the fixed-cycle model has **not yet been established as their root cause**.

## Goal

**Implement hardware-grounded, instruction-dependent CPU cycle accounting for both emulated machine profiles**, rather than applying a blanket speed multiplier or tuning a constant until a particular game feels faster.

- **PC-9801VM profile:** NEC V30 timing, using the relevant NEC documentation and validated hardware behavior.
- **PC-9821Ap DOS profile:** target i486-family timing (including the appropriate internal vs external/bus clock relationship), based on Intel documentation and model-specific assumptions.

The timing model must distinguish architectural instruction execution, physical bus/wait-state costs and the existing device scheduler. Document which effects are exact, conditional, approximated or not yet modeled; do not label a coarse approximation as cycle-accurate.

## Implementation scope

- [ ] Establish and document the target CPU variants, clock domains, memory/bus assumptions and authoritative timing references for each profile.
- [ ] Change the CPU execution API to report **cycles actually consumed** per instruction or bounded execution unit, separately from the number of instructions/REP elements retired. Propagate that elapsed time through `Machine` instead of unconditional `bus.tick(8)`.
- [ ] Provide per-profile, instruction-/operand-form-dependent timing: register vs memory operands, addressing modes, prefixes, taken/not-taken branches, shifts/multiply/divide, calls/returns, and other supported instructions.
- [ ] Account for **REP/string operations** by actual element count and setup/iteration costs, including interruption boundaries; preserve bounded stepping and interrupt-shadow correctness.
- [ ] Model memory and I/O timing where applicable (RAM vs VRAM, port I/O, bus width/alignment, wait states, and relevant i486 cache hit/miss effects). Treat any undocumented assumptions as explicit testable approximations rather than silently charging a flat cost.
- [ ] Account for interrupt/exception entry, fault/retry behavior, HLT/idle time and any firmware-assisted transfers without double-counting elapsed time.
- [ ] **Separate CPU clocks from device/scheduler clocks** and convert elapsed time consistently for PIT, RTC, GDC/vertical sync, FDC/IDE, FM/PCM sound, mouse and IRQs. Do not assume that an i486 CPU core clock is the same as the peripheral clock.
- [ ] Revisit the browser worker's instruction-count budgets and audio-driven pacing after cycle accounting changes. Keep guest-time progression consistent with wall-clock/audio playback without creating underruns or unbounded catch-up.
- [ ] Expose useful diagnostics: retired instructions, CPU cycles, device/guest elapsed time, instruction throughput and screen-transition duration.

## Verification / acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deterministic unit tests compare documented V30 and i486 instruction classes and operand variants against their respective reference timing tables, including conditional paths and REP lengths.
- [ ] Bus/VRAM/I/O, interrupts, HLT and multi-clock-domain conversion tests assert expected elapsed cycles and device events; CPU clocks must not be mistaken for the existing 8 MHz scheduler clock.
- [ ] Existing VM and Ap guest, protected-mode, paging, device, sound and browser/Wasm regression tests still pass.
- [ ] Compare representative guest workloads against documented or measured target-hardware timings where feasible (including image decode/VRAM transfer and game screen transitions). Record deviations and any remaining unmodeled microarchitectural behavior.
- [ ] Verify BGM pitch/tempo, PIT/IRQ cadence and frame timing remain correct when CPU throughput changes.
- [ ] Remove or explicitly isolate the fixed 8-clock instruction fallback; no silent fixed-cost treatment of supported instructions that are claimed to be accurately timed.

## Related work

- #136 — browser worker execution/audio decoupling
- #138 — game audio playback/validation

This is a **CPU/hardware timing accuracy issue**, not simply a performance optimization: real-time browser throughput and faithful emulated elapsed time need to be measured separately.", "url": "https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/issues/140", "created_at": "2026-11-06T09:40:03Z", "state": "OPEN", "repository": "takahirox/pc98-rust", "labels": ["task"], "priority": null, "status": "In Progress", "is_archived": false}, "context": {}, "resources": {}, "allocation": {}, "instruction": null, "run_id": "896bb3dad32748dfbf278a9ba2f3671b"}
